entities.summary:
Pope Benedict IV, bishop of Rome and ruler of the Papal States from February 1, 900, until his death in July 903, emerged as a figure of restorative authority during the tumultuous *Saeculum obscurum*, a period marked by profound political instability and moral challenges for the Roman See. Succeeding Pope John IX, Benedict IV sought to re-establish papal legitimacy following the scandal of the Cadaver Synod and the subsequent rapid succession of pontiffs. His brief pontificate is noted for its attempt to bring stability to the Church amidst competing Roman factions and the encroaching influence of secular powers.

During his reign, Benedict IV undertook several significant actions to consolidate papal authority and navigate the complex political landscape of early 10th-century Europe. Most notably, he crowned Louis III the Blind as Holy Roman Emperor on February 15, 901, an act symbolizing the enduring, albeit often contested, partnership between the papacy and the imperial power. He also continued the work of his predecessor in rehabilitating the memory of Pope Formosus, reversing the condemnations of the Cadaver Synod and restoring the ordinations performed by Formosus, thereby attempting to heal a profound schism within the Roman clergy. Additionally, he excommunicated the rebellious Count Adalbert II of Tuscany for his opposition to the emperor.
